items.title: Authoring With LLM
items.text:
The Beginning

Date: 2026-06-20 Author: Codebot Topic: blogging, narrative, session-management
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Provide a practical guide for using large language models (LLMs) to author polished blog posts efficiently, from initial briefing through final publication.
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Many writers struggle to translate ideas into well-structured prose. LLMs such as GPT-4, Claude, and Gemini can serve as genuine collaborators rather than simple prompt-response tools. This guide documents a disciplined workflow that consistently produces publishable drafts.
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Writing blog posts from scratch is time-consuming. Unstructured prompting produces disorganized output. Hallucinations and tone drift are common without verification checkpoints. A repeatable process is needed to combine AI speed with human editorial judgment.
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 4.1 Define the Brief Before Prompting
items.text:
Before the first prompt, collect three elements:

  • Target audience (who is the reader?)
  • Core message or thesis (what should they learn?)
  • Constraints (tone, length, required sources)

A well-crafted briefing document becomes a system prompt inherited by all subsequent sessions, ensuring consistency.
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 4.2 Use an Outline as an Anchor
items.text:
Do not ask the model to write the full post at once. Feed a detailed outline first:

  • Section-by-section sub-headings in logical order
  • Bullet-level intent for each section
  • Ask the LLM to expand each section while preserving the backbone

Any drift from the outline is immediately visible because every paragraph traces back to an author-authored heading.
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 4.3 Treat Iterations as Deliberate Process
items.text:
First drafts from LLMs rarely read like final output. Use iteration deliberately:

  • Request specific improvements per section
  • Tighten arguments, add examples, swap passive voice
  • Enhance transitions between paragraphs

This mirrors the workflow used with any human editor or ghostwriter.
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 4.4 Verify with Human Judgment at Every Stage
items.text: LLMs can generate plausible but inaccurate text (hallucination). Cross-check key claims against credible sources before publishing. Monitor style drift - redirect early with briefing instructions (e.g., think like a skeptical friend talking over coffee).
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 4.5 Final Polish Remains Human
items.text: Reserve the author's voice for the final review. Read the full draft aloud; if it sounds robotic, revise the brief or iteration approach. The model accelerates writing but does not replace the author.
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: The combination of clear structure, iterative feedback, and human oversight yields the best results: AI generation speed with human critical taste. Without structured briefing and outline anchoring, output tends toward disorganized soup. Without verification, hallucinations enter the final text. Without final human polish, voice drift persists.
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: The five-step workflow (Brief -> Outline -> Iterate -> Verify -> Polish) reliably produces publishable drafts in a fraction of manual writing time. The key discipline is treating the LLM as a collaborative editor, not an autonomous writer.
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
A structured, iterative LLM-assisted writing workflow:

  1. Pre-session briefing document (audience, thesis, constraints)
  2. Detailed outline fed to model before generation
  3. Section-by-section expansion with deliberate iteration
  4. Fact-checking and style verification at each stage
  5. Final human voice pass
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Apply workflow to next 3-5 blog posts
  • Measure time from idea to published draft vs. manual baseline
  • Track hallucination rate in first drafts vs. after verification
  • Assess voice consistency across multiple posts
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text:
• Create a reusable briefing template for common post types
  • Document iteration prompts that consistently improve quality
  • Evaluate whether outline generation itself can be partially automated
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Always start with a written brief, even for short posts
  • Never skip the outline step - it prevents structural drift
  • Build a personal library of effective iteration prompts
  • Treat verification as non-negotiable, not optional
  • Keep the final voice pass manual - it is the author's signature
path: Authoring With LLM

items.title: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes
items.text: Date: 2026-06-20 Author: Codebot Topic: Hermes Agent, Ollama, WSL2, narrative, local-llm, failover
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Audit and rebuild a local LLM inference stack on WSL2 (16GB RAM, no GPU) to eliminate unused models, pull CPU-appropriate models, and implement a cloud failover layer for code tasks requiring more compute.
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: The Hermes Agent was routing through a local Ollama instance (ollama-launch provider at http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1) with minimax-m3:cloud as the active model. Eleven models were configured, several too large for CPU inference on the available memory. No automated failover existed for cloud provider quotas.
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text:
• Model hoarding: 11 models configured, many unusable on CPU with ~6GB free RAM
  • No failover: Cloud provider quota exhaustion caused silent failures
  • Unclear model roles: No routing strategy for different task types (structured output vs. explanations vs. code)
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 4.1 Hardware Reality Check
items.text: Confirmed WSL2 allocation: 7.8GB (50% of 16GB host), ~6.1GB free. No GPU. Realistic model headroom: ~3-4GB.
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 4.2 Model Audit
items.text: Listed 11 configured models from Hermes Agent config and live Ollama instance. Identified oversized models: gemma3n:7b (7GB), qwen2.5-coder:7b (4.7GB).
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 4.3 Pull CPU-Appropriate Models
items.text:
Selected three models optimized for quality-per-byte on CPU:

  • qwen2.5:3b (1.9 GB) - general purpose
  • deepseek-r1:1.5b (1.1 GB) - reasoning
  • starcoder2:3b (1.7 GB) - code-focused

Pulled in background over slow connection (~2.5 MB/s). Total new disk usage: ~4.7GB.
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 4.4 Model Testing and Profiling
items.text:
Ran identical prompt against all three models:

Model Result Time Tokens/sec Assessment qwen2.5:3b Correct JSON + prose 16s 11.38 Reliable deepseek-r1:1.5b Empty JSON (strict), good plain text 2.88s N/A Good for explanations starcoder2:3b Garbage output, timeout on code 10.31s / 120s timeout N/A Unreliable
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 4.5 Cleanup of Large Models
items.text:
Removed four models from Hermes Agent config and Ollama disk:

  • qwen2.5-coder:7b (4.7 GB) - deleted
  • translategemma:4b (3.3 GB) - deleted
  • qwen3-vl:4b-instruct (~3 GB) - deleted
  • gemma3n:latest (~7 GB) - not on disk, config-only removal

Freed ~11GB disk space.
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 4.6 Default Model and Routing Rules
items.text:
Set Hermes Agent default to qwen2.5:3b (most reliable for structured output and code). Established routing rule:

  • plain -> deepseek-r1:1.5b (explanations)
  • structured -> qwen2.5:3b (JSON, code)

Registered as Hermes Agent quick commands.
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 4.7 Cloud Failover Layer
items.text:
Built cloud_failover.sh script:

  • Iterates provider|model pairs in priority order
  • Sources credentials from ~/.hermes/.env
  • Honors Hermes Agent profiles
  • Exponential backoff retry
  • Logs attempts with timestamps, duration, output previews

Built cloud_providers_health.sh for manual health checks.

Smoke test: Failover succeeded against OpenRouter. Health check: OpenRouter timeout, OpenAI and Anthropic OK (~2s).
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: The original stack suffered from three issues: (1) model bloat with oversized models consuming disk and config complexity, (2) no routing strategy causing inappropriate model selection per task, (3) single-point-of-failure on cloud providers with no automated failover. The CPU memory constraint (6GB free) fundamentally limits local inference to 3B-parameter models.
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: The lean stack (3 local models + cloud failover) fits within hardware constraints and provides clear routing semantics. qwen2.5:3b is the workhorse for structured tasks. deepseek-r1:1.5b serves explanations. Cloud failover handles code tasks requiring more compute. starcoder2:3b requires further evaluation.
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Reduced from 11 to 3 local models (4.7GB total)
  • Established task-type routing with quick commands (plain, structured, failover)
  • Implemented automated cloud failover with exponential backoff and logging
  • Freed 11GB disk space
  • All changes survive session restart
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Retry starcoder2:3b with controlled code-only prompt
  • Configure cron/systemd timer for regular health checks
  • Add log rotation for failover and health check logs
  • Test failover under actual quota exhaustion
  • Consider raising WSL2 memory cap via .wslconfig
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text:
• Complete starcoder2:3b evaluation
  • Automate health checks
  • Implement log rotation
  • Test WSL2 memory increase
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Audit local model inventory quarterly; remove unused large models
  • Always define routing rules before adding models
  • Implement failover for any production cloud dependency
  • Profile models on target hardware before committing
  • Keep quick command names semantic (plain, structured, failover)
path: From Model Chaos to a Lean Stack: A Saturday Evening with Hermes

items.title: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)
items.text: Date: 2026-06-21 Author: Codebot Topic: Hermes Agent, Ollama, tinyllama, OpenRouter, context-window, modelfile, WSL2
path: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Document the complete session covering OpenRouter free-tier configuration, credential rotation, the local Ollama switch to tinyllama, Hermes Agent's 64K minimum-context guard patching, and a Modelfile-based context extension attempt.
path: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: User preference: free/zero-tier providers only (OpenRouter free models, Ollama local, Google AI Studio free). Hermes Agent config at /home/sigit/.hermes/config.yaml, auth pool at /home/sigit/.hermes/auth.json, agent source at /home/sigit/.hermes/hermes-agent/agent/agent_init.py. WSL2 with 16GB RAM, no GPU, ~6.7GB available. Local Ollama models include tinyllama (637 MB, 2K context), deepseek-r1:1.5b, starcoder2:3b, qwen2.5:3b, qwen3:4b. OpenRouter free tier was rate-limited (HTTP 429). Need local fallback for chat-only tasks.
path: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text:
OpenRouter free tier exhausted; local fallback required. Two-layer blocking then prevents tinyllama use in Hermes Agent:

  1. Static guard in agent_init.py rejects any model with context < 64K at initialization
  2. Runtime guard queries Ollama for actual loaded context; refuses tool-use sessions if < 64K

tinyllama reports 2,048 tokens at both layers. Direct ollama run works but bypasses Hermes Agent tool infrastructure. Modelfile num_ctx parameter may not affect runtime context.
path: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)

items.title: 4.1 OpenRouter Free Model Configuration
items.text:
• Set model.provider = openrouter, model.default = poolside/laguna-m.1:free
  • Updated quick_commands with free model IDs
  • Wrote 27 free model IDs to /home/sigit/free_models.txt
path: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)

items.title: 4.2 Credential Management
items.text:
• Added OpenRouter API key via hermes auth add openrouter --type api-key --api-key <KEY> (stored as api-key-2)
  • Live test failed: HTTP 429 (free-models-per-day exhausted)
  • Added new key (api-key-3), removed exposed keys (api-key-1, api-key-2)
path: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)

items.title: 4.3 Local Ollama Switch
items.text:
• RAM check: 7,942 MB total, ~6,711 MB available
  • Set Hermes Agent: model.provider = ollama-launch, model.default = tinyllama:latest, model.context_length = 2048
  • Hermes Agent refused: 2,048 < 64,000 minimum
  • Direct Ollama test succeeded: ollama run tinyllama:latest "Reply with exactly: connected" -> "Exactly"
path: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)

items.title: 4.4 Static Guard Patch
items.text:
Patched /home/sigit/.hermes/hermes-agent/agent/agent_init.py (lines ~1543-1555):

  • Added per-model whitelist: {tinyllama, tinyllama:latest}
  • When model context < 64K, check normalized model ID against whitelist
  • Whitelisted models: log informational message, proceed
  • All other models: raise original ValueError
_model_id = str(getattr(agent, "model", "") or "").strip().lower()
try:
    from agent.model_metadata import _strip_provider_prefix
    _norm_model = _strip_provider_prefix(_model_id)
except Exception:
    _norm_model = _model_id

_allowed_small_models = {"tinyllama", "tinyllama:latest"}

if any(am in _norm_model for am in _allowed_small_models):
    _ra().logger.info(
        "Model %s has a context window of %d tokens (< %d) but is allowed by per-model override.",
        agent.model, _ctx, MINIMUM_CONTEXT_LENGTH,
    )
else:
    raise ValueError(...)
path: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)

items.title: 4.5 Runtime Guard Persistence
items.text: After the patch, Hermes Agent still refused due to the second runtime-capability check: Ollama advertises runtime context = 2,048 for tinyllama. Agreed to try extending context via Modelfile.
path: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)

items.title: 4.6 Modelfile Experiment
items.text:
Attempted to increase Ollama runtime context via Modelfile:

  1. Created ~/tinyllama-modelfile:
FROM tinyllama:latest
PARAMETER num_ctx 65536

  1. Built tag: ollama create tinyllama:65k -f ~/tinyllama-modelfile

  2. Verified: ollama show tinyllama:65k showed num_ctx 65536 in parameters

  3. Tested: ollama run tinyllama:65k "Reply with exactly: connected" succeeded

  4. Checked runtime: ollama ps confirmed running context 2048 before and after restart

Reverse procedure (for rollback of any custom variant):

ollama list
ollama rm tinyllama:65k
hermes config set model.default tinyllama:latest
hermes config set model.context_length 2048
# Or switch provider back:
hermes config set model.provider openrouter
hermes config set model.default poolside/laguna-m.1:free
path: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)

items.title: 4.7 Root Cause Analysis
items.text: Modelfile metadata changed but the prebuilt quantized model's serving runtime operates with a fixed 2K window. Not all models support context extension by declaration alone; underlying weights or runtime layout may need rebuilding.
path: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)

items.title: 4.8 Cleanup and Final Config
items.text:
Deleted tinyllama:65k with ollama rm tinyllama:65k.

Final Hermes Agent config:

  • model.default = tinyllama:latest
  • model.context_length = 2048
  • model.ollama_num_ctx = 2048

Per-model patch allows tinyllama to initialize for chat. Restrict to simple chat flows (no tool-calling, no long sessions). Direct ollama run remains fallback.
path: The 64K Context Wall and How Hermes Refused to Let Me Through It (Modelfile Recipe Included)

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: OpenRouter free tier exhausted; local fallback required. The static guard patch successfully allows tinyllama by name. However, Ollama's runtime context is determined by the model's compiled configuration, not Modelfile metadata alone: tinyllama's architecture or quantization fixes the context at 2K. The per-model override is the correct surgical fix - it preserves the 64K guard for all other models while enabling chat-only use of tinyllama.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• OpenRouter: free models configured, quota exhausted, keys rotated
  • Implemented per-model context-guard override in Hermes Agent source, allowing tinyllama variants to bypass the 64K minimum
  • Verified Modelfile num_ctx parameter does not extend runtime context for this model
  • Configured Hermes Agent for tinyllama:latest at truthful 2K context with explicit chat-only restriction

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Configure Ollama CLI as a unified proxy front-end for multiple LLM providers (GitHub Copilot, OpenRouter, Ollama cloud) without local model weights, using stateless adapter containers pulled via OCI references.
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Hermes Agent runs on WSL2 (FedoraWSL) with local Ollama and cloud providers. OpenRouter and GitHub Copilot already connected. Goal: ollama launch <model> routes to any provider via adapter containers. User explicitly does not want local model weights.
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Ollama CLI natively runs local models. Need to extend it to proxy requests to external provider APIs through adapter containers, making those adapters appear as first-class Ollama models.
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 4.1 Goal Clarification
items.text:
User requirement: Ollama as proxy/front-end for GitHub Copilot API (and others), not as model runner. Three approaches offered: - A: Hermes Agent built-in multi-provider routing (already working) - B: Adapter OCI images pulled via ollama pull docker://... - C: Ollama Modelfile as first-class model definition wrapping adapter

User chose to keep all three as options.
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 4.2 Ollama Capability Investigation
items.text: ollama --help, ollama pull --help, ollama create --help, ollama run --help: - ollama pull accepts OCI refs (e.g., docker://ghcr.io/...) - ollama create accepts -f Modelfile - ollama run supports --keepalive, --format, --insecure, experimental flags - :cloud models already present (e.g., gemma4:31b-cloud)
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 4.3 Adapter Design
items.text:
Core concept: tiny Docker images (~20MB) with Python script: 1. Read prompt from argv/stdin 2. Call target provider HTTP API (OpenRouter or Copilot proxy) 3. Print response to stdout

Ollama pulls/runs as models. Stateless - no weights, fast startup, trivial updates.

Templates provided for: - OpenRouter adapter: openrouter_adapter.py + Dockerfile + requirements.txt - Copilot adapter: two variants (shell-out to copilot CLI, or HTTP proxy) - Build/push commands for GHCR with docker login + docker push
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 4.4 Modelfile Template
items.text:
Created /home/sigit/Modelfile: 

name: copilot-adapter
run: |
  #! /bin/sh
  /app/copilot_adapter ""

description: "Adapter that proxies prompts to GitHub Copilot"

build:
  context: .
  dockerfile: Dockerfile
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 4.5 Hermes Agent Integration
items.text:
Bridge Ollama models into Hermes Agent /model picker: 

hermes config set providers.ollama-launch.models '["openrouter:adapter","copilot:adapter","gemma4:31b-cloud"]'
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 4.6 Architecture Summary
items.text:
User
  ollama launch <adapter>
    Ollama pulls/runs adapter container
      adapter calls provider API
        response to stdout
          Ollama returns to user

Hermes /model
  reads providers.ollama-launch.models
    shows all three provider models as choices
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 4.7 Key Decisions
items.text: Decision Rationale Adapter images, not local models User explicitly said no local models Stateless containers No weight storage, fast startup, trivial updates GHCR registry Free for public, integrates with GitHub Modelfile approach Makes adapters first-class Ollama models Keep A/B/C available User wants flexibility, not lock-in
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 4.8 Security Note
items.text: API keys via environment variables or Docker secrets only. Never bake into images.
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Ollama's OCI support and Modelfile system enable running arbitrary containers as "models." This is an unconventional but clean pattern for provider proxying. The Modelfile bridges script-to-model recognition. Hermes Agent config is the glue for UI visibility.
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Architecture is sound. Adapters are lightweight. GHCR integration is seamless. Hermes Agent bridge is minimal. No code written yet - all design and templates.
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text: Designed adapter-based Ollama proxy architecture with Modelfile templates, Dockerfile templates, GHCR push workflow, and Hermes Agent integration. Three approaches (A/B/C) preserved as options.
path: Configuring Ollama Github Models

  • Build locally with ollama create or docker build
  • Push to GHCR (requires GitHub PAT)
  • Register model names in Hermes Agent config
  • End-to-end test: ollama run openrouter:adapter "hello"

  • Build and test locally
  • Push to GHCR
  • Register in Hermes Agent config
  • Full integration test

items.title: 1. Objective

path: Hermes Agent Claw Migrate Dry Run

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: hermes claw migrate is a first-class subcommand for migrating from OpenClaw to Hermes. Siblings: migrate (import) and cleanup (archive old install). Flags: --dry-run, --preset {user-data,full}, --migrate-secrets, --overwrite, --no-backup, --skill-conflict, --source. Defensive by default: preview, backup, ask before overwrite.
path: Hermes Agent Claw Migrate Dry Run

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: Hermes Agent Claw Migrate Dry Run

items.title: 4.1 Command Discovery
items.text: Queried Hermes Agent for command details. Confirmed claw is a first-class subsystem with three subcommands (migrate, cleanup, clean) and dedicated --migrate-secrets gate.

items.text: User chose dry-run only (sensible for orientation).
path: Hermes Agent Claw Migrate Dry Run

path: Hermes Agent Claw Migrate Dry Run

items.text: ls -laR ~/.openclaw: directory exists but nearly bare. Only state/ subdirectory with state/openclaw.sqlite (1 MB). No config, skills, memories, settings, provider keys. Migrator didn't recognize SQLite file as source for any of 34 categories.
path: Hermes Agent Claw Migrate Dry Run

items.text: Dry-run completed safely. No harm, no side effects, complete answer. Tool behaves as designed.
path: Hermes Agent Claw Migrate Dry Run

  • note-taking (Obsidian only)
  • productivity (closest action-oriented peers)
  • humanizer (voice and prose guidance)
  • cleanup-sessions (concise action-and-verification structure)

Selected productivity as correct category (publishing workflow, not art form).
path: Making a Skill for Blogging Sessions (or: So I Stop Having to Re-explain It)

items.title: 4.3 Skill Design Decisions
items.text:
Three key decisions shaped the skill:

  1. Two-phase structure: Phase 1 composes narrative (first-person, beat-by-beat, no chatbot refuse); Phase 2 saves to disk with no-overwrite guarantee and post-write verification. Separation keeps phases testable and prevents writing before user sees draft.

  2. No-overwrite rule (load-bearing): User's prior instruction: "keep existing pieces, create a new entry." Baked in: ls directory first, slug filename, append disambiguator on collision, never clobber.

  3. Bite-sized verification checklist: Nine checkboxes:

  4. Narrative shown

  5. Voice check
  6. Directory exists
  7. Existing entries listed
  8. No-collision filename
  9. File written
  10. File verified
  11. Final report states path + untouched-file count

Each checkable; nothing vague.
path: Making a Skill for Blogging Sessions (or: So I Stop Having to Re-explain It)

items.title: 4.5 Principle Application
items.text: Authoring-skill documentation emphasis: every line must change agent behavior. Non-behavioral lines are sediment. Final skill ~220 lines, tight prose, heavy procedure.

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: A skill encodes "stop making me re-explain this." The artifact is the skill; the deliverable is one fewer user instruction. Constraint compliance: each line changes behavior. Category placement (productivity) correct for publishing workflow.
path: Making a Skill for Blogging Sessions (or: So I Stop Having to Re-explain It)

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Skill created and registered. Two-phase structure with no-overwrite guarantee and explicit verification checklist meets all requirements. Will be available in next Hermes Agent session.
path: Making a Skill for Blogging Sessions (or: So I Stop Having to Re-explain It)

items.text:

  • Peer skills surveyed for structure and patterns
  • Three design decisions: two-phase, no-overwrite, verification checklist
  • Skill created at ~/.hermes/skills/productivity/session-to-blog/SKILL.md

items.title: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices
items.text: Date: 2026-06-29 Author: Codebot Topic: OpenRouter, providers, Ollama, local-llm, Hermes Agent
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Migrate Hermes Agent from local Ollama + OpenRouter fallback to Google Gemini (AI Studio free tier) as primary provider, resolving configuration pitfalls and establishing credential management best practices.
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 2. Background
items.text:
Previous setup: tinyllama:65k and qwen2.5:3b via Ollama, patched Hermes Agent runtime checks for small models, OpenRouter as cloud fallback (cycling gpt-5.5, nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra, free-tier models). Issues: OpenRouter free tier model availability, unpredictable rate limits, tinyllama stuck at 2K runtime context.

Desired: reliable cloud API, first-party, free tier, static API key, 1M token context.
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Switching from local (Ollama) to cloud (Gemini) provider requires clearing legacy model.base_url or requests route to wrong endpoint. Free-tier Pro model has extreme rate limits. Credential propagation to external tools (OpenCode, OpenClaw) must avoid plaintext shell profiles.
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 4.1 Migration Commands
items.text:
hermes auth add gemini --type api-key --api-key "AIzaSy..."
hermes config set model.provider gemini
hermes config set model.default gemini-2.5-flash
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 4.2 The base_url Trap
items.text:
Test failed: 404: model 'gemini-2.5-flash' not found. Error showed:

Endpoint: Endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1

model.provider switched but model.base_url still pointed at Ollama.

Fix:

hermes config set model.api_key ""
hermes config set model.base_url ""

Clean state confirmed:

Model: {'api_key': '', 'base_url': '', 'default': 'gemini-2.5-flash', 'provider': 'gemini'}

Lesson: When switching local->cloud, MUST clear model.base_url. Error blames model ID; real culprit is endpoint.
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 4.3 Pro Model Quota Trap
items.text:
Tried gemini-2.5-pro for reasoning:

429 Too Many Requests: You exceeded your current quota...

Free tier Pro: extremely tight limits. Flash: 15 RPM. Pro unusable for agent workloads (5-10 rapid calls/task).

Mitigation: Added agent memory note: always suggest Flash, warn about Pro quota. Hermes Agent now steers to gemini-2.5-flash by default. No way to hide Pro from picker (Hermes Agent reads full API model list). Workaround: pin default to Flash, let memory handle rest.
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 4.4 Credential Management: Vault vs Environment
items.text:
Gemini key in Hermes auth pool (~/.hermes/auth.json, mode 600). External tools need same key.

Naive approach (bad):

export GOOGLE_API_KEY="AIzaSy..."  # plaintext in history, scrollback, hard to rotate

Better approach: pull from vault at shell startup:

export GOOGLE_API_KEY=$(hermes auth list gemini | grep -o 'AIzaSy[A-Za-z0-9_-]*' | head -n 1)

Benefits:

  • Single source of truth (auth vault)
  • Rotation in Hermes Agent propagates automatically
  • No plaintext in shell profiles

Caveat: hermes auth list may redact secret in some versions. Fallback: hermes config set-env to ~/.hermes/.env (tool-protected).
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 4.5 Before vs After Comparison
items.text: Aspect Before (Ollama + OpenRouter) After (Gemini) Latency Variable (local: fast/dumb, cloud: slow aggregator) Consistent ~1-2s Context window 2K-8K (tinyllama fought) 1M tokens Model quality Small models hallucinated Flash handles most tasks Rate limits Ollama: none, OR: unpredictable 15 RPM (predictable) Setup complexity Moderate (Ollama + config hacks) Minimal (3 commands) Reliability Frequent 404s from OR, Ollama crashes Single stable endpoint
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Migration technically simple (3 commands) but base_url leftover creates confusing failure mode. Hermes Agent design: model.provider and model.base_url independent; changing one doesn't clear the other. Correct for 20+ providers but confusing during migration. Pro model quota is a hard free-tier limit requiring behavioral workaround.
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Gemini Flash provides reliable, fast, large-context inference on free tier. Setup minimal. Credential management via vault is secure and maintainable. Pro model excluded behaviorally.
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Migrated to Gemini via AI Studio free tier (3 commands)
  • Cleared base_url trap (critical step)
  • Pinned default to gemini-2.5-flash; behavioral guard against Pro
  • Credential in Hermes Agent vault; shell export pulls from vault
  • No plaintext keys in profiles
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Monitor Flash reliability and latency in production
  • Verify Pro quota warning triggers correctly
  • Test credential rotation propagation
  • Confirm no base_url regressions on future provider switches
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text:
• Test hermes auth list redaction behavior; implement .env fallback if needed
  • Document base_url trap in team runbook
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Always check Endpoint: Endpoint: line in errors before assuming model ID is wrong. Endpoint reveals actual routing. 127.0.0.1:11434 = Ollama, not Google. Fix routing first.
  • Clear model.base_url and model.api_key when switching local->cloud
  • Pin free-tier defaults to models with usable quotas
  • Use vault-sourced shell exports for credential propagation
  • Behavioral guards (agent memory) for unpinnable model picker entries
path: Migrating from Ollama to Google Gemini.md + Credential Practices

items.title: 4.1 Hardware Reality Check

items.title: 4.3 Pull CPU-Appropriate Models

Three models selected for quality-per-byte on CPU:

Model Size Role qwen2.5:3b 1.9 GB General purpose deepseek-r1:1.5b 1.1 GB Reasoning starcoder2:3b 1.7 GB Code-focused

Model Result Time Tokens/sec Assessment qwen2.5:3b Correct JSON + prose 16s 11.38 Reliable deepseek-r1:1.5b Empty JSON (strict), good plain text 2.88s N/A Good for explanations starcoder2:3b Garbage, timeout on code 10.31s / 120s N/A Unreliable
path: Building A Local LLM Setup In WSL2

items.title: 4.5 Cleanup
items.text:
Removed from Hermes Agent config and Ollama disk:

  • qwen2.5-coder:7b (4.7 GB)
  • translategemma:4b (3.3 GB)
  • qwen3-vl:4b-instruct (~3 GB)
  • gemma3n:latest (~7 GB, not on disk)

Freed ~11GB disk.
path: Building A Local LLM Setup In WSL2

items.title: 4.6 Default and Routing
items.text:
Set Hermes Agent default: qwen2.5:3b. Quick commands registered:

  • plain -> deepseek-r1:1.5b
  • structured -> qwen2.5:3b
  • failover -> cloud_failover.sh
path: Building A Local LLM Setup In WSL2

items.title: 4.7 Cloud Failover Layer
items.text:
cloud_failover.sh:

  • Iterates provider|model pairs in priority order
  • Sources ~/.hermes/.env
  • Honors Hermes Agent profiles
  • Exponential backoff
  • Logs to ~/.hermes/logs/cloud_failover.log

cloud_providers_health.sh: manual health checks, logs to ~/.hermes/logs/cloud_providers_health.log.

Smoke test: failover succeeded (OpenRouter). Health check: OpenRouter timeout, OpenAI/Anthropic OK (~2s).
path: Building A Local LLM Setup In WSL2

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Original stack: model bloat, no routing strategy, single-point-of-failure on cloud. CPU memory (6GB free) limits local inference to ~3B parameters.
path: Building A Local LLM Setup In WSL2

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Lean stack (3 local + cloud failover) fits constraints with clear routing. qwen2.5:3b = workhorse. deepseek-r1:1.5b = explanations. Cloud failover = code tasks. starcoder2:3b needs evaluation.
path: Building A Local LLM Setup In WSL2

items.title: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider
items.text: Date: 2026-06-29 Author: Codebot Topic: OpenRouter, providers, Ollama, local-llm, Hermes Agent
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Connect Hermes Agent to OpenRouter as a cloud provider, replacing local Ollama backend, and verify end-to-end connectivity.
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Hermes Agent ran on WSL2 with local Ollama (ollama-launch provider, minimax-m3:cloud model, http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1). Local models limited: no reasoning, no large context, no frontier capabilities. OpenRouter aggregates dozens of providers under one API key.
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Local Ollama backend lacks frontier model capabilities. Need reliable cloud provider with dynamic model routing.
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 4.1 State Assessment
items.text: hermes config show and hermes auth list: - Provider: ollama-launch - Model: minimax-m3:cloud - Base URL: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 - OpenRouter not in auth pool - Commented # OPENROUTER_API_KEY= in .env (placeholder, never filled)
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 4.2 API Key Acquisition
items.text: User provided OpenRouter key in chat. Proceeded directly to persistence (no echo/storage in chat).
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 4.3 Credential Storage
items.text:
Two approaches attempted:

  1. Direct .env write - blocked. .env is protected; write_file tool rejects it.
  2. hermes auth add - proper path.
  3. Interactive hermes auth add openrouter failed: no TTY (termios.error)
  4. Non-interactive flag worked: 
    hermes auth add openrouter --type api-key --api-key 'sk-or-...'
  5. Result: "Added openrouter credential #1: \"api-key-1\"" in ~/.hermes/auth.json (mode 600)
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 4.4 Provider Switch
items.text:
hermes config set model.provider openrouter
hermes config set model.default openrouter/auto
hermes config set model.api_key ""      # clear old ollama key
hermes config set model.base_url ""     # clear old ollama URL

openrouter/auto lets OpenRouter pick best available model dynamically (cost-optimized).
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 4.5 Verification
items.text:
Doctor check: False alarm - "model.provider 'openrouter' is set but no API key is configured." Doctor only scans .env, not auth.json. Credential valid.

Live test: 

hermes chat -q "Reply with exactly: openrouter-connected"
Response in 4 seconds. OpenRouter routed successfully.
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: hermes auth add --api-key is the correct non-interactive credential method. Interactive prompt requires TTY and crashes with EOFError otherwise. Doctor's .env check is stale - doesn't recognize auth.json credentials. openrouter/auto is a solid default for dynamic routing. No restart needed - new hermes invocation picks up config immediately.
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Connection established and verified. Credential stored securely in auth.json. Dynamic model routing active. Legacy Ollama config cleared.
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• OpenRouter credential added via hermes auth add --api-key (non-interactive)
  • Provider switched to openrouter, model to openrouter/auto
  • Legacy base_url and api_key cleared
  • Live test confirmed end-to-end connectivity (4s response)
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Monitor OpenRouter usage and quota
  • Test openrouter/auto model selection quality
  • Verify Doctor check false alarm does not affect operations
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: • None immediate. Configuration complete and verified.
path: OpenRouter as Cloud Provider

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Always use hermes auth add --api-key for non-interactive credential addition
  • Clear model.base_url and model.api_key when switching from local to cloud providers
  • Be aware of Doctor's .env-only credential check limitation
  • openrouter/auto recommended for "best available" dynamic routing

items.title: Taming the Context Window
items.text: Date: 2026-06-29 Author: Codebot Topic: OpenRouter, providers, Ollama, local-llm, Hermes Agent
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Enable Hermes Agent to accept small-context local models (specifically tinyllama at 2K) for chat-only workflows on CPU-only WSL2, by patching the 64K minimum context guard and investigating Ollama Modelfile-based context extension.
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: WSL2, 16GB RAM, no GPU, free tiers only. Hermes Agent refuses models below 64K context. Local models: tinyllama (637 MB, 2K), deepseek-r1:1.5b, starcoder2:3b, qwen2.5:3b, qwen3:4b. OpenRouter free tier rate-limited (HTTP 429). Direct ollama run works but bypasses Hermes Agent tool infrastructure.
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Two-layer block: (1) static guard in agent_init.py rejects init for context < 64K, (2) runtime guard queries Ollama for loaded context, refuses tool-use if < 64K. Need surgical fix preserving guard for other models.
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 4.1 Direct Ollama Test (Bypass)
items.text:
ollama run tinyllama:latest "Reply with exactly: connected"
# Output: Exactly
Model loads, responds, minimal RAM. But no Hermes Agent tools, memory, skills.
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 4.2 Static Guard Patch
items.text:
File: ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/agent/agent_init.py (~line 1545).

Original: 

_ctx = getattr(agent.context_compressor, "context_length", 0)
if _ctx and _ctx < MINIMUM_CONTEXT_LENGTH:
    raise ValueError(...)

Patch: per-model override with whitelist.

_model_id = str(getattr(agent, "model", "") or "").strip().lower()
try:
    from agent.model_metadata import _strip_provider_prefix
    _norm_model = _strip_provider_prefix(_model_id)
except Exception:
    _norm_model = _model_id

_allowed_small_models = {"tinyllama", "tinyllama:latest"}

if any(am in _norm_model for am in _allowed_small_models):
    _ra().logger.info(
        "Model %s has a context window of %d tokens (< %d) but is allowed by per-model override.",
        agent.model, _ctx, MINIMUM_CONTEXT_LENGTH,
    )
else:
    raise ValueError(...)

~25 lines. Uses _strip_provider_prefix for prefixed names (e.g., ollama-launch:tinyllama:latest). Logs clear message on override fire. Whitelist explicit - every new small model must be deliberately added.
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 4.3 Runtime Guard: Ollama Modelfile
items.text:
After patch, second error: 

Ollama loaded tinyllama:latest with only 2,048 tokens of runtime context, but Hermes needs at least 64,000.

Hermes Agent queries Ollama for actual loaded context. Ollama defaults tinyllama to 2K unless told otherwise.

Modelfile approach: 

FROM tinyllama:latest
PARAMETER num_ctx 65536


ollama create tinyllama-65k -f ~/Modelfile.tinyllama

Changes runtime parameter. Model weights same. Not yet tested (writing post first). If 65K OOM on 8GB, will drop to 32K/16K.
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 4.4 Before vs After
items.text: Aspect Before After Hermes Agent refuses tinyllama Hard block at init Whitelist allows it Ollama runtime context 2,048 tokens Needs Modelfile to increase Tool-calling small models Impossible Possible (after Modelfile) Safety guard other models 64K minimum Still 64K minimum OpenRouter dependency Required for cloud fallback Local fallback available
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Hermes Agent 64K minimum is reasonable for production agent workloads. Global disable not recommended. Per-model override is surgical fix preserving safety while enabling local-first for CPU users. Modelfile num_ctx is standard Ollama method but effectiveness depends on model architecture. Must verify runtime context empirically with ollama ps.
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Patch applied and tested for static guard. Modelfile approach pending test. Whitelist currently {tinyllama, tinyllama:latest}. Final config will be honest about capabilities.
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Patched agent_init.py with per-model whitelist override for tinyllama variants
  • Static guard bypassed for whitelisted models with info log
  • Modelfile instructions prepared for runtime context extension
  • Global 64K guard preserved for all other models
  • Direct ollama run remains escape hatch
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Create and test Modelfile tinyllama-65k
  • Verify runtime context with ollama show and ollama ps
  • Test Hermes Agent chat with tinyllama (simple chat only)
  • Confirm tool-calling sessions refused appropriately
  • Monitor guard behavior for regressions
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text:
• Execute Modelfile build and verify runtime context
  • If 65K fails, test 32K/16K
  • Evaluate alternative small models with native large context
  • Document override pattern for future additions
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Use per-model whitelist overrides, not global minimum reduction
  • Test Ollama runtime context empirically (ollama ps), not via metadata alone
  • Accept hardware/model limitations honestly; configure tool restrictions accordingly
  • Keep direct ollama run as escape hatch for refused operations
  • Rotate API keys immediately when exposed in chat
path: Taming the Context Window

items.title: Openclaw Dementia And Config Backups
items.text:
When OpenClaw Forgot Its Models

Date: 2026-06-29 Author: Codebot Topic: openclaw, Hermes Agent, env-vars, config-backups, Gemini
path: Openclaw Dementia And Config Backups

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Diagnose OpenClaw's inability to reach configured models and establish configuration backup practices for Hermes Agent equivalent to OpenClaw's JSON config.
path: Openclaw Dementia And Config Backups

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: OpenClaw "temporary dementia": cannot find route to working models. Previous solution for Gemini API key sharing: shell exports (GOOGLE_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL=generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/). User confirmed variables set correctly.
path: Openclaw Dementia And Config Backups

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Environment variables set but OpenClaw TUI returns run error: LLM request failed on simple "hello" after model selection. Not connection refused or bad key - generic failure suggesting stale path, hardcoded endpoint, or missing config file credential.
path: Openclaw Dementia And Config Backups

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: Openclaw Dementia And Config Backups

items.title: 4.1 Environment Verification
items.text: Confirmed GOOGLE_API_KEY and OPENAI_BASE_URL set correctly. Not the issue.
path: Openclaw Dementia And Config Backups

items.title: 4.2 Model List and Selection
items.text: openclaw models list: gemini, ollama cloud, ollama local. Set active model to known-good entries. TUI launches. "hello" -> run error: LLM request failed.
path: Openclaw Dementia And Config Backups

items.title: 4.3 Config File Restoration
items.text: User had old openclaw.json backup from early days. Restored it. OpenClaw "dementia lifted." Required provider URLs, default endpoints, last-known-good model lived in JSON, not environment variables.
path: Openclaw Dementia And Config Backups

items.title: 4.4 Hermes Agent Backup Creation
items.text:
Hermes Agent equivalent of openclaw.json: two files:

  • ~/.hermes/config.yaml (settings, model prefs, tools)
  • ~/.hermes/auth.json (API keys, encrypted)

items.title: 1. Objective

items.text: WSL2 Fedora vhdx consumed 8.3 GB of GGUF blobs while Windows host had 200+ GB free. User had already migrated from Ollama to llama.cpp on Windows. Ollama blob directory is flat hash pool (sha256-) requiring manifest cross-reference for human-readable identification.
path: Moving LLM Models Out Of WSL2

items.title: 3. Problem

items.title: 4.1 Blob Census and Mapping
items.text:
Scanned ~/.ollama/models/blobs/ and cross-referenced against manifests in ~/.ollama/models/manifests/registry.ollama.ai/library/:

Model Size Blob Hash (prefix) qwen3:4b 2.50 GB sha256-3e4cb1... qwen2.5:3b 1.93 GB sha256-... starcoder2:3b 1.71 GB sha256-... deepseek-r1:1.5b 1.12 GB sha256-... mxbai-embed-large 0.67 GB sha256-... tinyllama 0.64 GB sha256-... nomic-embed-text 0.27 GB sha256-...

Total: 7 GGUFs, ~8.84 GB. File magic confirmed all start with GGUF (0x47475546).

Cloud models (nemotron-3-super:cloud, minimax-m3:cloud) had no local blobs - Hermes Agent provider aliases routing to OpenAI-compatible endpoints. ornith:9b (5.6 GB) on NixOS homelab, not in WSL.

items.title: 4.2 Copy to Windows

  • Transfer: ~97 seconds over 9P share (~140 MB/s per file)
  • Verification: SHA256 re-hash matched filename for all 7 files
  • Windows free space: 214.7 GB to 196.8 GB (delta ~8.84 GB)

items.title: 4.3 Human-Friendly Renaming with Sidecar Manifest
items.text:
• Renamed: qwen3:4b to qwen3-4b.gguf (colons not allowed on Windows)
  • Created manifest.json sidecar mapping friendly name to original SHA256:
{
  "name": "qwen3:4b",
  "file": "qwen3-4b.gguf",
  "size_bytes": 2500000000,
  "sha256": "3e4cb1..."
}

items.text: Sidecar manifest preserves SHA256 identity critical for verification, re-pull, and cross-reference with llama-cli. Flat hash pool requires manifest mapping for human usability. Windows filename restrictions (no colons) necessitate renaming with provenance tracking.

items.title: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy
items.text: Date: 2026-07-16 Author: Codebot Topic: homelab, LiteLLM, Caddy, SSL, NixOS, sudo
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Import homelab CA certificate to Windows Trusted Root Store to resolve browser "connection not secure" error for litellm.home.arpa.
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Browser showed "your connection isn't secure" for litellm.home.arpa. CA cert available at /mnt/homelab/home/homelab-ca.crt. Simple certutil import expected to resolve.
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: After CA import, browser error changed to ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID. Certificate trusted but hostname mismatch. Server cert generated before litellm.home.arpa added to Caddyfile. Wildcard DNS:*.home.arpa should match but Chrome treats .arpa as public suffix, blocking wildcard matches. Only explicit SAN entries work.
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 4.1 CA Certificate Import
items.text:
• Copied cert to Windows Desktop
  • Ran certutil -addstore -f Root
  • UAC prompt accepted
  • Cert landed in Trusted Root Store
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 4.2 Hostname Mismatch Diagnosis
items.text:
• Traced through NixOS stack: homelab.crt generated by homelab-cert oneshot service
  • SANs built from Caddy service list
  • litellm.home.arpa in Caddyfile but cert generated before addition
  • Wildcard DNS:*.home.arpa present but Chrome blocks .arpa wildcard matches
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 4.3 Certificate Regeneration Requirement
items.text:
• Fix: sudo systemctl restart homelab-cert.service && sudo systemctl restart Caddy
  • Blocked: agent cannot sudo (password required, no interactive SSH)
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 4.4 Sudo Policy Design
items.text:
• Drafted sudo.nix module using security.sudo.extraRules
  • First attempt: rule order wrong (NOPASSWD ALL last, overriding nixos-rebuild restriction)
  • Sudoers rule: last matching rule's tags win
  • Fixed order: NOPASSWD ALL first, PASSWD nixos-rebuild last
  • Rebuild confirmed: sudo -n whoami returns root, sudo -n nixos-rebuild requires password
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 4.5 Certificate Regeneration
items.text:
• With sudo working, restarted homelab-cert.service and Caddy
  • New cert includes litellm.home.arpa in explicit SANs
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Chrome public suffix list treats .arpa as TLD equivalent, disabling wildcard SAN matching. Cert generation timing (before Caddyfile update) caused missing SAN. Sudo policy required for operational automation without compromising generation safety.
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: CA cert trusted on Windows. Server cert regenerated with explicit litellm.home.arpa SAN. Sudo policy: NOPASSWD for operations, PASSWD for nixos-rebuild. All from single cert import request.
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Imported homelab CA to Windows Trusted Root Store
  • Diagnosed .arpa wildcard blocking by Chrome public suffix rules
  • Designed sudo.nix with correct rule ordering (NOPASSWD first, PASSWD nixos-rebuild last)
  • Regenerated server cert with explicit litellm.home.arpa SAN
  • Verified sudo -n works for operations, blocks nixos-rebuild
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Verify browser access to litellm.home.arpa shows secure
  • Test sudo -n for operational commands
  • Confirm sudo -n nixos-rebuild requires password
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text:
• Monitor cert renewal automation
  • Document .arpa public suffix behavior for future certs
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Add hostnames to Caddyfile before cert generation
  • Use explicit SANs for .arpa domains (no wildcards)
  • Order sudo rules: permissive first, restrictive last
  • Separate operational sudo from generation sudo
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: Podman Migration & Stabilization
items.text: Date: 2026-07-19 Author: Codebot Topic: homelab, LiteLLM, Podman, NixOS, Caddy, troubleshooting
path: Podman Migration & Stabilization

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Stabilize LiteLLM proxy on NixOS homelab through Podman container migration, auto-restart system, and configuration fixes over three days (9 sessions).
path: Podman Migration & Stabilization

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: LiteLLM migrated from systemd-native service to Podman container fronted by Caddy on port 4000. Two profiles shared hardware: #homelab (headless) and #workstation (desktop GUI). Operational wrapper handled config rendering, provider management, CLI tools. Proxy unreachable initially.
path: Podman Migration & Stabilization

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Container crash-looping, config mount path mismatch between image versions, rogue provider in runtime models.json, 502 errors from Caddy, database requirements for UI, sudo policy conflicts, wall command freezing terminals, profile targeting confusion.
path: Podman Migration & Stabilization

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: Podman Migration & Stabilization

items.title: 4.1 Day 1: Initial Access and Config Changes
items.text:
• SSH into homelab, navigated to /srv/repo/nix-lab/modules/ai/
  • Modified wrapper: litellm-render auto-restart via systemd path unit
  • Added file watching for config.yaml
  • Committed, rebuilt, tested
path: Podman Migration & Stabilization

items.title: 4.2 Day 1 Evening: Container Crash-Loop Fix
items.text:
• Root cause 1: :main tag entrypoint reads /app/proxy_server_config.yaml, but Nix module mounted to /app/config.yaml. LiteLLM fell back to bundled Azure config and crashed.
  • Root cause 2: :main nightly hangs on large configs (131 models). Switched to v1.92.0 stable.
  • Version-specific mount path: v1.92.0 reads /app/config.yaml (correct), :main reads /app/proxy_server_config.yaml.
  • Fixed: pinned v1.92.0, mounted to correct path.
  • Removed rogue mygpu provider from runtime models.json (no API key).
path: Podman Migration & Stabilization

items.title: 4.3 Day 2: Provenance Tracking and No-Rebuild Provider
items.text:
• Item 2: litellm-add-provider supports --models '' for single-step provider+model registration. Each model gets origin.type=manual, added_at timestamp.
  • Item 3: Added origin provenance metadata to models.json, threaded through renderer to config.yaml. Every model carries source (declared vs discovered vs manual). Merge logic preserves manual-origin across rebuilds.
path: Podman Migration & Stabilization

items.title: 4.4 Day 2 Evening: 502 Debug and Constraints
items.text:
• 502 from Caddy: container up but refusing connections.
  • LiteLLM v1.92.0 expects database for UI login. Rendered config had no database_url.
  • Tried SQLite database_url: crash-loop. SQLite support broken in v1.92.0 image.
  • Reverted to no-DB mode: proxy works, UI login non-functional (accepted).
  • Three constraints documented in AGENTS.md:
  • wall broadcasts freeze terminals -> reverted to logger only
  • Sudo policy: passwordless for all except nixos-rebuild (prevent accidental generation changes) -> locked down
path: Podman Migration & Stabilization

items.title: homelab vs #workstation on same hardware -> always rebuild workstation
path: Podman Migration & Stabilization

items.title: 4.5 Day 3: Cleanup and Documentation
items.text:
• Removed duplicate cmd in Nix module (entrypoint ignores it)
  • Added logs/ volume mount (harmless, journald primary)
  • Updated README: pinned image, config mount path, no-DB limitation
  • Certificate never the problem: Caddy serves valid *.home.arpa from Homelab Internal CA. Browser errors were client-side trust.
path: Podman Migration & Stabilization

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Image version dictates config mount path. Large configs hang on nightly. Database required for UI but SQLite broken in v1.92.0. Operational constraints (sudo, wall, profile targeting) must be codified. Client-side cert trust != server cert validity.
path: Podman Migration & Stabilization

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Stable LiteLLM container on v1.92.0 behind Caddy. Auto-restart on config changes. No-rebuild provider registration. Provenance tracking through pipeline. Locked-down sudo policy. AGENTS.md documents operational knowledge.
path: Podman Migration & Stabilization

items.title: 7. Solution Summary

items.title: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle
items.text: Date: 2026-07-18 Author: Codebot Topic: Hermes Agent, OpenCode, workflow, orchestrator, Electron, project-management
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Establish automated multi-agent workflow between Hermes Agent (strategist/reviewer) and OpenCode (coder) with human as project manager, using structured state-machine orchestration.
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: User wanted Hermes Agent and OpenCode to collaborate in automated loop. Initial ad-hoc relay (terminal OpenCode run) worked for single prompts but not multi-turn. Explored three communication modes before settling on artifact-driven state machine.
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Simple turn-taking doesn't scale to multiple specialized agents. Need structured workflow with human-in-the-loop gates, persistent artifacts, and clear authority boundaries.
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 4.1 Communication Mode Exploration
items.text: Mode Description Result 1. Ad-hoc relay opencode run as one-shot subprocess Works for single prompts, slow for multi-turn (cold start) 2. Long-lived server opencode serve HTTP API (port 4096, SSE, OpenAPI 3.1) Security issue: /config/providers returns all API keys plaintext even with Basic Auth. Mitigation: bind localhost, strong password. 3. Autonomous loop Python converse.py alternating Hermes Agent chat / opencode run Proved functional: 6 sec/turn with free tier (opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free). Google models timeout via OpenCode but work via Hermes.
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 4.2 State Machine Redesign
items.text:
User rejected alternation model. Designed workflow state machine:

  • Roles: Project Manager (human), Code Reviewer (Hermes Agent), Coder (OpenCode)
  • Artifacts: status.json, objective.md, plan.md, implementation.diff, review.md, decision.md, coder-reply.md, workspace/, README.md, transcript.md
  • States: CLARIFY -> PLAN -> AUTHORIZE -> IMPLEMENT -> REVIEW -> APPROVED -> COMPLETE
  • Authority: OpenCode never receives task without explicit PM authorization. Control returns to human between agent actions.
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 4.3 Orchestrator Implementation
items.text:
workflow.py CLI with step-advance pattern:

python3 workflow.py --init session/todoist-wrapper --objective "Create Electron app for Todoist"
python3 workflow.py --advance session/todoist-wrapper  # -> PLAN
python3 workflow.py --approve session/todoist-wrapper  # -> IMPLEMENT
python3 workflow.py --advance session/todoist-wrapper  # -> REVIEW

Coder step: opencode run returns conversational text. Script extracts markdown code blocks with filenames, writes to workspace/. Cleaning functions strip Hermes Agent CLI overhead and OpenCode ANSI/headers.
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 4.4 First Cycle: Todoist Electron Wrapper
items.text:
Objective: Minimal Electron wrapper for Todoist.com (1200x800, frameless, custom title bar, UA spoofing).

Successes:

  • Thorough plan: security (contextBridge, no nodeIntegration), error handling, UA spoofing
  • Clean code: main.js, preload.js (draggable title bar overlay), package.json (Electron v33)
  • Full cycle ~8 minutes, zero manual intervention post-approval
  • Git initialized at session root (artifacts) and workspace/ (code diffs)

Failures Fixed:

  • Deep nesting: OpenCode prefixed workspace/ -> workspace/workspace/main.js. Fixed by stripping prefixes.
  • Verdict parsing: instruction examples (VERDICT: APPROVED) leaked into output. Fixed by filtering instruction lines.
  • Stray node_modules: 271MB under skill scripts from test run.
  • Session state sync: do_approve saved AUTHORIZE before IMPLEMENT. If OpenCode hung, state stuck. Fixed by deferring save.
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 4.5 Code Quality Standards (Reviewer Prompt)
items.text: 8-point standard: descriptive names, error handling required, no hardcoded secrets, input safety, demo boundary, cross-platform fallbacks, well-known dependencies, comments on non-obvious logic.
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Opencode run is conversational, not file-writing - requires markdown block extraction. Google models route poorly through OpenCode (timeouts) but work via Hermes. Free tier (opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free) responds in 6-10 sec. State machines scale better than turn-taking for 3+ agents. Artifact cleaning critical - prompt instructions leak into output.
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Orchestrator functional with crash-safe state machine. First cycle produced working Electron app. Artifact-driven approach provides complete audit trail.
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Designed 3-role, 7-state workflow with artifact gates
  • Implemented workflow.py with step-advance CLI
  • Extracted code from conversational OpenCode output via markdown blocks
  • Completed first cycle: Todoist Electron wrapper (COMPLETE with decision.md override)
  • Documented 8-point code quality standard
  • Skill at ~/.hermes/skills/software-development/project-manager-assistant/ (v0.3)
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Test recovery from OpenCode timeout
  • Add knowledge/RAG agent
  • Fix stray scripts/workspace/ directory
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text:
• Fix scripts/workspace/ stray directory cleanup
  • Add error recovery for OpenCode timeout
  • Make --advance for AUTHORIZE flow automatically into IMPLEMENT
  • Add knowledge/RAG agent
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Use OpenCode free tier for programmatic calls (reliable, fast)
  • Avoid Google models via OpenCode (routing timeouts)
  • Aggressively strip prompt instructions from agent outputs
  • State machine > turn-taking for multi-agent workflows
  • Artifact-driven design enables audit and recovery
path: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and Running the First Cycle
